notes: In Kaş, cash (TL) is still preferred at tradesmen's restaurants and village markets. Cards sometimes fail in small places, so carry cash.
The main transport within town and between villages is the dolmuş (minibus). Services are infrequent, so plan your evening so you don't miss the last one.
Tipping 5-10% of the bill is common in restaurants but not obligatory. On boat tours, a small extra tip for the captain and crew is expected.
A light shawl covering shoulders and knees is useful at ancient cities and castles. On beaches with stairs such as Kaputaş, non-slip shoes are essential.
In July the midday heat (12:00-16:00) is very high. During these hours, choose shade or the sea, reapply sunscreen often and drink plenty of water.
When negotiating with private boatmen (Blue Cave, Limanağzı), settle the price before boarding and ask whether it is per person or per boat.
In villages such as Üzümlü, Pınarbaşı and Çukurbağ, ask permission before entering locals' gardens or taking photos.

niche.name: Elden Ne Gelir Ceramic Workshop
niche.why_hidden: The workshop of ceramicist Sibel Düzel, who has worked alone for 22 years in Pınarbaşı village, right at the foot of ancient Phellos. It is an art pocket completely outside Kaş's 'diving and boat tour' image, and appears in no classic travel guide.
niche.access_instructions: About 20 minutes by private car from central Kaş via Çukurbağ village to Pınarbaşı; the last 500 metres are an unsigned forest road. If you turn up without notice, the owner may not be home, and the workshop door is usually closed.
niche.local_contact: Instagram @eldennegelir (DM ile en az 1 gün önceden randevu iste)
niche.season: April-October (in winter the village road and workshop sometimes close)
niche.insider_tip: Before your visit, say you want to shape a piece with your own hands. Sibel Düzel serves tea in the garden of the house below the workshop and explains the production process; she will fire the piece you choose and ship it to you.
niche.show_reason: Kaş'ın turistik tekne-plaj rutininin tam zıttı: antik bir kentin içinde, tek bir ustanın elinden çıkan sanat üretimini görme şansı; hem tarihi hem yaratıcı katman bir arada.
niche.address: Pınarbaşı Mahallesi, Phellos Antik Kenti yamacı, Kaş, Antalya

days.theme: Kaş signature day: ancient harbour and turquoise pebbles

stops.name: Antiphellos Ancient Theatre
stops.tips: The only ancient theatre in Anatolia right on the sea, with free entry. On the way out, stop by the huge Lycian rock tomb just above Uzun Çarşı. Go around 9:30 to see it in peace before the tour buses arrive.

stops.name: Bi'Lokma Bahçe
stops.tips: A family-run place in Andifli Mahallesi serving home cooking since 2001. Try the karnıyarık (stuffed aubergine), mantı (Turkish dumplings) and hünkar beğendi (lamb on smoky aubergine purée), and ask for a seat in the green garden. Arrive around 12:30, before the crowds.

stops.name: Big Pebble Beach
stops.tips: Kaş's signature pebble beach, within walking distance of the centre. Bring your own towel and you skip the sunlounger fee; municipal sunloungers cost about 150 TL.

stops.name: Uzun Çarşı
stops.tips: Handmade sandals, silver jewellery and boutique shops, with room for bargaining. Late afternoon light is best for photos.

stops.name: Smileys Restaurant
stops.tips: Inside Kaş Marina, they catch their own fish by rod. Ask for the catch of the day and request a table with a marina view; booking is recommended.

stops.name: Meis (Kastellorizo) Island Viewpoint
stops.tips: A waterfront strip you can walk from central Kaş; watch the lights of the Greek island come on across the water. Completely free, and a romantic way to end the day.

backups.name: Taşbahçe
backups.tips: A spread-style breakfast and lunch table with sugar-free marmalade, acuka (walnut and pepper paste) and plenty of olives. Head here if Bi'Lokma is full.

backups.name: Small Pebble Beach
backups.tips: If Big Pebble is crowded, move to this small cove closer to the town centre. The water is calm and it suits families.

days.theme: Kekova boat tour: sunken city, Gökkaya and Simena

stops.name: Kekova Boat Tour (Sunken City, Gökkaya Bay, Kaleköy Castle)
stops.tips: Departs from Kaş Fishing Harbour; includes 5 swim stops and lunch. When the boat anchors at Kaleköy, leave time for the path up to the castle: entry is about 190 TL, paid separately (Museum Pass not valid). Board early and try to grab a shaded spot by the jetty.

stops.name: Kaş Marina Evening Walk
stops.tips: A good way to ease tired feet after the tour. The moored boats are lit up and the ice cream shops are open.

stops.name: Deniz'in Sesi Balıkçısı
stops.tips: Fresh fish and regional meze by the sea. Try the stuffed mussels and the catch of the day, and ask for a table on the waterfront.

backups.name: Ehlikeyf Meyhane
backups.tips: Known for its evening entertainment and meze. If Deniz'in Sesi is full, come here for a rakı and fish table.

backups.name: Üçağız
backups.tips: A quiet fishing village in the Kekova area. The tour boat may stop here too, and it makes a good break for tea on the wooden jetty.

stops.name: Kaputaş Beach
stops.tips: Reached by a 187-step staircase; entry is about 60 TL per person. Go early for a spot: the free parking pockets along the road fill up fast.

stops.name: Blue Cave Boat Tour
stops.tips: A small boat hired by negotiation from a boatman at Kaş harbour. The cave can only be entered by sea and the visit takes 15-20 minutes. Midday is best for the play of light.

stops.name: Limanağzı Bay
stops.tips: A few minutes by boat from Kaş harbour: neighbouring calm bays with no waves. At the small beach tavernas you can eat fresh köfte or fish in a bread roll; the price covers the boat and lunch.

stops.name: Türkmen Sofrası
stops.tips: A tradesmen's restaurant run by Nedim and his family, on the main road from the mosque to the bus station. Ask for the home-cooked dish of the day: good value and filling.

stops.name: Panorama Viewpoint Hill
stops.tips: Kaş's best-known sunset spot: by day you look out to Meis Island, by night to its lights. It can be crowded, but the view is worth it.

backups.name: Helios Meyhane
backups.tips: Kaş breakfast plus meze and fish in one place. A good evening alternative if Türkmen Sofrası is closed.

backups.name: Aquarium Bay
backups.tips: If Limanağzı is hard to reach, head to this clear cove in the same area. It is reached by boat and you can see the seabed very clearly.

days.theme: Kaş underwater and the Çukurbağ Peninsula

stops.name: Kaş: Scuba Diving Experience
stops.tips: An instructor-led trial dive in Kaş, considered Türkiye's diving capital; equipment, boat and insurance are included. For those without a licence, you get a 20-25 minute underwater trip at about 5 metres depth.

stops.name: Maşuk Meyhane
stops.tips: Known on Liman Sokak for its süt balık (milk-poached fish) and lentil piyaz (lentil salad). Ideal for a light but filling lunch after your dive, and lunchtime prices are lower than in the evening.

stops.name: Çukurbağ Peninsula
stops.tips: A coastal road winding between boutique guesthouses, with quiet coves away from the tourist rush. Explore on foot; entry is completely free.

stops.name: Demeti Meyhane
stops.tips: With its garden ringed by lemon trees, it is ideal for summer evenings. The meze selection is rich and booking is recommended.

backups.name: Hideaway
backups.tips: Serves spread-style breakfast and light lunches at cushioned tables. Come here if Maşuk is full.

backups.name: Gökkaya Bay
backups.tips: Reached on a short boat trip from the boatmen. You can swim in the pirate cave, and it is a quiet alternative to Çukurbağ.

days.theme: Ancient Phellos and art in a mountain village

stops.name: Phellos Ancient City Walk
stops.tips: A climb of about 30 minutes on a forest path via Çukurbağ village. Sturdy shoes and plenty of water are essential, and there are almost no crowds.

stops.name: Elden Ne Gelir Ceramic Workshop
stops.tips: The workshop of Sibel Düzel, who has been making ceramics for 22 years in Pınarbaşı village, on the slope below Phellos. Let her know in advance via Instagram, or you may find the door closed.

stops.name: Kaş Köy Sofrası
stops.tips: Set in nature on the Sarıbelen road. A spread table full of village cheese, olives, jam and fresh gözleme (stuffed flatbread).

stops.name: Voyn Meyhane
stops.tips: In Andifli Mahallesi, with seafood and breakfast plates in one place. Try the artichoke with pistachios and the rum-flavoured prawns.

backups.name: Çınarlar Kahvaltı Evi
backups.tips: A calm lunch stop with a large garden. If Köy Sofrası feels too far, switch to this alternative close to the town centre.

backups.name: Kaş King's Tomb (Lycian Rock Tomb)
backups.tips: If you can't book the workshop, take time to study the huge Lycian sarcophagus above Uzun Çarşı in detail. Completely free and central.

days.theme: Patara Valley: Xanthos, Saklıkent and Patara Beach

stops.name: Xanthos Ancient City
stops.tips: The UNESCO-listed Lycian capital, about 1 hour from Kaş by dolmuş or car. Entry is separately ticketed, and there is more shade early in the day.

stops.name: Saklıkent Canyon
stops.tips: One of Europe's deepest canyons, ranking second, with a wet crossing where you hold onto a pole. Rent water shoes; the water is ice cold.

stops.name: Ayşe Pancake House
stops.tips: A family-run gözleme place in Gelemiş village. Ideal for a hearty meal after the canyon; try the herb and cheese gözleme.

stops.name: Patara Beach & Ancient City of Patara
stops.tips: Türkiye's longest beach (18 km), woven together with ancient ruins. The entry fee (about 15€) covers both the archaeological site and the beach. Shade is scarce, so bring a hat and umbrella.

backups.name: Cafe Inn Patara
backups.tips: A small but tasty cafe in Gelemiş. If Ayşe Pancake House is full, come here for breakfast items or a light lunch.

backups.name: Letoon Ancient City
backups.tips: A UNESCO-listed sanctuary very close to Xanthos. If Xanthos is crowded or closed, go here instead: it is quieter to explore.

days.theme: Kalkan and Üzümlü village: farewell tour

stops.name: Üzümlü Village Gözleme Houses
stops.tips: A vineyard village above Kalkan, famous for thin sac-griddled gözleme that taste like a mother's touch and for homemade jams. There is no signboard, so ask at the café on the village square and they will point you the way.

stops.name: Kalkan Old Town
stops.tips: Cobbled streets draped in bougainvillea. The boutique shops allow some bargaining, and in the midday heat the shaded streets are the better choice.

stops.name: Kalkan Public Beach
stops.tips: A Blue Flag municipal beach with completely free entry. It has small pebbles, so water shoes will come in handy.

stops.name: Salonika 1881 Restaurant
stops.tips: Among the stone streets, known for its homemade burgers and meze. Ideal for a farewell lunch, and calm early in the day.

backups.name: Cafe Del-Mar
backups.tips: A practical choice for lunch in central Kalkan. If Salonika 1881 is full, come here.

backups.name: Kalamar Bay
backups.tips: If Kalkan Public Beach is crowded, head to this bay with pedalos and canoes. The entry fee is included in the activities.
